title: Homogeneity of Electro-Mechanical and Optical Characteristics in Ring-Shaped MEMS Shutter Arrays with Subfield Addressing for Interference Microscopy
content: We present a MEMS-array-based approach for micro irises called “ring shutter”, utilizing subfield addressing for applications in advanced micro-optics such as interference microscopy. The study is focused on investigating the homogeneity of electro-mechanical and optical characteristics within and between subfields of a lab demonstrator device. The characterisation aims to ensure cross-talk-free and swift optical performance demonstrated in a previous study. For this purpose, the transmission in the initial state, actuation voltages, and response dynamics are measured per each electrode as well as for the whole device and thoroughly compared. The measurements are conducted by expanding an existing optical actuation setup via tailored 3D-printed apertures al-lowing the isolation of selected rings and zones. Evaluation of measurement data confirms the stable and cross-talk free operation of the ring shutter. Both angular and radial homogeneity are robust and follow the expectations in the experiment. While transmission, actuation voltage and closing time slightly rise (up to 25%) with increased radial position represented by five ring sec-tions A – E, the characteristics for the three angular zones 1 – 3 remain nearly constant. Response times are measured below 40 µs, actuation voltages do not exceed 60 V, and the overall transmis-sion of the ring shutter yields 53.6%.
